## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.89); key evidence e2, e3, e5.

Why: Massive tubulin increase with mitotic arrest and 7/10 stabilizer atlas neighbours leaves stabilizers far ahead.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Washout regrowth plus EB1 comet / tubulin polymer vs soluble fraction to confirm stabilized microtubules, and phospho-H3 FACS for mitotic arrest.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean profile comparison across all 8 conditions. Requires revising local rule to reflect score variance.

## Unblinding

Compound: **latrunculin B** (PubChem CID [6436219](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6436219))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

## Reflection

Unblinded as latrunculin B with truth Actin disruptors, my Microtubule stabilizers call at p=0.89 was wrong. I was driven by e2 at 10 uM with extreme tubulin signals tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.6, tub_mean z=+50.0, tub_std z=+43.2, reinforced by e5 with 7/10 atlas neighbours as Microtubule stabilizers and e3 microscopist candidate as Microtubule stabilizers.

What I missed is that actin depolymerization, now well established for latrunculin B (PMID 19800245, PMID 41208085, PMID 41951336), causes cell rounding, compaction and detachment that can artifactually concentrate tubulin signal and inflate intensity and texture metrics. I interpreted e2 tubulin increase plus e4 nuclear shape change nuc_solidity z=-18.3 as mitotic stabilization without ever testing an actin-collapse alternative.

My acquisition choices locked in the error: I acquired only two wells at 10 uM and 1 uM, relied on tubulin and nuclear features alone with no F-actin readout, and used compare_to_reference_atlas to confirm rather than discriminate stabilizer versus actin-disruptor morphology.

What was right:
- Detected a potent dose-dependent perturbation with lower density vs DMSO in e3 and 252 cells at 10 uM in e2 versus 702 cells at 1 uM in e4
- Detected strong cytoskeletal disturbance in tubulin channel in e2 and nuclear shape change in e4, correctly flagging a cytoskeleton-active compound

What was wrong or missed:
- Mistook massive tubulin intensity and texture increases in e2 tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.6, tub_mean z=+50.0 for microtubule stabilization without considering actin-loss rounding/compaction artifact
- Over-relied on e5 7/10 stabilizer atlas neighbours and e3 candidate Microtubule stabilizers without testing actin-disruptor hypothesis
- Acquired only 2 wells at 10 uM and 1 uM with no low-dose morphology and no actin-specific measurement to separate actin collapse from true stabilized bundles

Proposed next experiment: Parallel dose-response with F-actin phalloidin vs alpha-tubulin co-staining plus soluble-versus-polymer tubulin fractionation and washout, with paclitaxel as stabilizer control and latrunculin A as actin-disruptor control, to test for actin loss and cell rounding without true stabilized microtubule bundles.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [19800245](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19800245/): Semisynthetic latrunculin B analogs: studies of actin docking support a proposed mechanism for latrunculin bioactivity. *Bioorg Med Chem* (2009) — Semisynthetic analog and docking work supports actin binding as the mechanistic basis for latrunculin B bioactivity.
- PMID [41208085](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41208085/): Actin depolymerization by Latrunculin B can either suppress or promote root gravitropism, depending on the developmental stages in Arabidopsis. *Plant Signal Behav* (2025) — Latrunculin B drives actin depolymerization in a biological system.
- PMID [41951336](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41951336/): Total Synthesis of Photoswitchable Latrunculin B Enables Reversible Control of Actin Polymerization and Cell Migration. *J Am Chem Soc* (2026) — Photoswitchable latrunculin B enables reversible control of actin polymerization and cell migration.
